dimensions.description: Measures whether the target manages a distributed footprint across multiple regions requiring standardized digital inspection tools.

disqualifiers: Companies with no active physical extraction, mining, or chemical refining sites in Latin America [3, 4].
Firms operating purely as commodity traders or distributors with no physical site infrastructure [2, 3].
Small-scale operators with total assets under $100M [3].
Operations that do not involve hazardous extraction or continuous 24/7 site processing [2, 4].
icp.notes:
Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile S.A. (SQM) is a major Chilean mining and chemical company [3] and a global leader in natural-source potassium nitrate and lithium production [2]. The company operates large-scale extraction and advanced chemical processing facilities across South America and globally across five continents [4]. SQM produces specialty plant nutrition, iodine, lithium derivatives (such as battery-grade lithium hydroxide), and industrial chemicals [2, 3, 4].

When reaching out to Site Directors, Head of Operations, or VP of HSE at target accounts, reference SQM's profile as a global lithium and chemical extraction leader [2, 3]. Highlight how FlytBase's Physical AI replaces contracted manual inspection crews at continuous, 24/7 hazardous extraction and refining sites [2, 4], directly supporting target initiatives around operational safety, low carbon footprints, and digital tool adoption [2, 4].

accounts.name: Codelco (Corporación Nacional del Cobre de Chile)

dimension_scores.rationale: World's largest copper mining enterprise, operating major open-pit and continuous underground extraction facilities.
Controls vast physical infrastructure across Chile including the Chuquicamata open pit, El Teniente underground mine, and massive tailings dams.
Operates continuous smelters, refineries, acid plants, and high-hazard tailings storage facilities requiring round-the-clock monitoring.
State-owned major generating over $15B annually with dedicated capital reserves for mine safety, automation, and infrastructure.
Operates seven distinct mining divisions distributed across northern and central Chile.
Pioneers continuous technology adoption including integrated remote operation centers (CIO) and autonomous haulage fleets.

accounts.fit_rationale:
Codelco perfectly matches the ICP given its massive multi-site copper footprint, continuous 24/7 hazardous refining operations, and enterprise financial scale. The high structural and environmental risks of its tailing dams and open pits make automated aerial inspection highly essential.

As Codelco refocuses on profitability, safety, and operational discipline under CEO Jorge Gómez and Chairman Bernardo Fontaine, improving operational efficiency while managing heavy debt and flat production is paramount. Autonomous drone inspection directly supports Codelco's fresh emphasis on field safety and operational discipline by removing personnel from hazardous site environments. Replacing manual monitoring with autonomous aerial inspections can reduce operational overhead and strengthen auditability across key mining operations.
